title: Social media
hook: post as if Christ were reading
tomorrow: Abuela prays all through the evening news. does it help anyone?

segments.voice: Yesterday, phones: Martha troubled about many things, Mary sitting with the guest, and one thing necessary, with the phone out of reach. The line was here, now.

A clip from the game: the other team's keeper slips, the ball rolls in, and somebody in the stands caught every second of it. It's funny, honestly. Everyone in the stands saw it anyway. A caption writes itself, and a clip like that could travel far by morning. The thumb is already on share. Post it or not? This is a choice from an ordinary week, and the tradition has a test for it that fits in a caption box.
screen: `THE KEEPER SLIPS.` → `A CAPTION WRITES ITSELF.` → `POST IT OR NOT?`

segments.voice: Paul wrote it long before anyone posted anything, in his letter to the Ephesians. In the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Let no evil speech proceed from your mouth; but that which is good, to the edification of faith, that it may administer grace to the hearers." Three tests in one verse. Is it good? Does it build up? Does it give something to the people who hear it? A post has more hearers than a mouth ever did. Jesus turns the same thing into a mirror: "All things therefore whatsoever you would that men should do to you, do you also to them." The keeper in the clip will see it too, or her little brother will. Pope Francis wrote that the digital world can be rich in humanity, a network not of wires but of people. That's the shift. The question stops being will it get views, and becomes who's on the other end. In Matthew, Jesus says that what's done to the least of his brethren is done to him. So the test in the outline, post as if Christ were reading, has a second edge: he's also the one in the clip. Would he post it isn't a ban on jokes. Plenty of funny things build people up. It's a pause long enough to see the person.
screen: `ONLY WHAT BUILDS UP.` · `DO AS YOU'D HAVE DONE.` · `A NETWORK OF PEOPLE.` · `HE'S ALSO THE ONE IN THE CLIP.` · then, large: `WOULD HE POST IT?`

segments.voice: Hold your phone in an open hand, screen dark, thumb resting off it. Bring to mind the last thing you posted or shared, and the faces of the people who saw it, one or two at a time. Ask of each one quietly: did it build them up? Then set the phone down, screen side down, and let your hands rest empty.
Social media. A crowd you can speak to in seconds, every word landing on a real person somewhere, including the one in the clip.
Your line: would he post it. A pause long enough to see the person on the other end. Till tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1650 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: ABUELA PRAYS ALL THROUGH THE EVENING NEWS. DOES IT HELP ANYONE?`

howItsDone: The Church marks a World Day of Social Communications each year, with a papal message on media; Catholics apply the eighth commandment and the golden rule to what they post.

do as you'd have done to you

myth: Paul says speech should build up and give grace to the hearers
Ephesians 4:29: that it may administer grace to the hearers.
the golden rule covers what you do, not what you post
all things whatsoever: a post is something done to someone.

he wrote that it can be rich in humanity: a network not of wires but of people.

fork.setup: your cousin's wedding toast went badly, and your aunt wants to post the video 'because it's hilarious.' what does today's test say?
options: ask your cousin first, and leave it unposted if it'd shame him.
post it; it's family, so teasing is part of the deal.
post it with a sweet caption so it comes off kind.
fork.reveal: Paul's test is what builds up the hearers, and your cousin is one of them. a kind caption doesn't change what the clip does to him.

original.note: Greek: building up. Paul's word in Ephesians 4:29, rendered edification in the Douay-Rheims.

trapdoor: what you thought: social media is fine as long as nothing you post is illegal.
what it means: every post lands on real people, so the test is whether it builds them up.
what a scholar hears: Ephesians 4:29 asks for speech that gives grace to the hearers, and Matthew 25:40 puts Christ among the least of them.
guess: a crowd you can speak to in seconds
a parish newsletter printed on paper
a private diary kept locked away

chat.says: rival keeper slipped, gave us a goal. teammate filmed it. caption: 'butterfingers.' post it? it's so funny
options: Skip it. She's a person who'll see it. Would he post it? Share the goal instead.
Post it. It's just a joke, and everyone knows keepers slip sometimes.
Post it on a private story so only your close friends see it.
chat.meaning: Paul's test: does it build up and give grace to the hearers? The keeper is one of the hearers. Would he post it?

Ephesians.meaning: Paul's letter to the Christians of Ephesus

edification.meaning: building someone up, in faith or in spirit

brethren.meaning: an old word for brothers, or brothers and sisters

Douay-Rheims.meaning: an old English Catholic translation of the Bible
